newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Senate to elect new president.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Senate to elect new president.

text.p: Brazil's Senate was due to choose a new president of the upper house later on Tuesday with a strong ally of the government widely expected to be elected to the two-year post, officials said.

Sen. Antonio Carlos Magalhaes, a former Bahia state governor and a stalwart of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso, looked set to win the secret ballot after receiving the support of Cardoso's Brazilian Social Democratic Movement Party (PSDB).
The election was due to begin at 2:30 p.m. local time (1630 GMT).
The president of the Senate is fourth in line in Brazil's political hierarchy and has the power to speed up or slow down the pace of bills passing through the upper house.
Magalhaes, of the government-allied Liberal Front Party (PFL), is running against Sen. Iris Rezende of the Brazilian Democratic Movement Party (PMDB), Congress' biggest party.

A PSDB spokeswoman said the party would back Magalhaes because it was supporting a candidate from the PMDB, Dep. Michel Temer, in an election for the presidency of the Chamber of Deputies, due to take place on Wednesday.
